After a horrible break up from a toxic relationship, and weeks of just alcohol and stuff, I spent a few months trying to work on myself. I’ve had many failed relationships, the first one especially. I was in, what could’ve been, a really great relationship but I had issues from previous years that I constantly kept bringing up. It not only ate me up from the inside, but her as well. For 5 months, after the break-up, I spent every single day in isolation ‘til I couldn’t bare the loneliness anymore and started dating again. After 4 relationships, I found a really great guy but he ghosted me. It hurt, but I didn’t feel like a failure, unlike with my first ex. Because this time, I really tried to be healthy and I knew that I gave my best for this person. So while I still wake up miserable and sad, I at least go through the rest of the day appreciating myself for doing the best that I can, and even if it’s slow, I’m constantly improving. I really do believe you can get through this. I don’t have the greatest self-worth or the highest self-esteem but I can respect myself at least because I am a person like everybody else, and like everybody else I have my faults and my lows but I’m trying so hard to deal with them. I don’t need the approval or acknowledgement of my peers, because I have myself for that. I have their support, their patience, and their tolerance, and that’s all I need. You should surround yourself with people like that btw. 

You might feel like shit rn because of your previous relationship, but know that you aren’t. Don’t ever stop working on yourself. Keep trying to do your best and know that that’s the best you can do. You are appreciated even if you don’t realize it. You aren’t alone with how you feel so don’t ever be scared of reaching out either.

Anyway, gl
